hero.intro: Equipment for transferring liquids and gases between storage and road tankers, rail cars and vessels: articulated top- and bottom-loading arms, marine and cryogenic arms, folding access stairs with safety cages, loading platforms, grounding and overfill monitors, metering skids and pigging systems. Each item is configured to the product, flow, connection and reach of your loading point and supplied from Dubai.

guidance.heading: Loading arm or hose?
guidance.body: A loading arm carries the product through rigid pipe and swivel joints, so the operator moves a balanced arm rather than lifting a heavy hose, and there is no hose to wear, kink or replace. Hoses remain the flexible, lower-cost choice for occasional transfers and for positions an arm cannot reach. Many terminals combine both: an arm at fixed bays and composite or rubber hoses for the rest.

service.heading: What to send for a loading-arm quote
service.body: Tell us the product (and its temperature), top or bottom loading, line size, the height and distance of the tanker connection from the arm's base, the connection at the tanker end (coupler, flange or drop pipe), any vapour return, and whether the bay is in a hazardous area. A sketch or photo of the bay helps.

items.q: What is the difference between top loading and bottom loading?
items.a: Top loading fills a tanker through its hatch from above with a drop pipe, so operators work on the tanker roof behind a safety cage or platform. Bottom loading connects a coupler to the tanker's bottom valves at ground level, which keeps operators off the roof and allows vapour recovery.

items.q: Why fit a safety cage or folding stairs at a loading bay?
items.a: They give operators a guarded working position on the tanker roof during top loading, reducing the risk of a fall from height. The folding stairs lower onto the tanker walkway and the cage surrounds the hatch area.

items.q: What does a grounding and overfill monitor do?
items.a: It confirms the tanker is earthed and stops the loading pump or valve if a compartment's overfill sensor trips, preventing static discharge and overfilling during bottom loading.

items.q: Can a loading arm be supplied for LNG or LPG?
items.a: Yes. Arms for cryogenic and pressurised gases are built with suitable swivels, seals and materials; send the product and design conditions so the arm can be specified for them.

hero.intro: Articulated loading arms transfer liquids and gases between fixed piping and road tankers, rail cars or vessels through rigid pipe and swivel joints. Top-loading arms fill through the tanker hatch with a drop pipe; bottom-loading arms connect to the tanker's bottom valves at ground level; marine arms connect a quay or jetty manifold to a ship. Arms are sized and balanced for each bay.

guidance.heading: Which loading arm?
guidance.body: Choose top loading for hatch filling and bottom loading where operators should stay at ground level or vapour must be recovered (a double arm carries liquid and vapour lines). PTFE-lined arms suit corrosive chemicals and food products; jacketed, heat-traced arms keep bitumen and viscous products fluid; cryogenic arms handle LNG, LPG and ammonia. Reach and connection height set the arm geometry.

service.heading: What to send
service.body: Product and temperature, line size, top or bottom loading, distances and heights from the arm base to the tanker connection, end connection, vapour return, balancing preference (spring, counterweight or cylinder) and hazardous-area classification.

items.q: What sizes of loading arm do you supply?
items.a: Road and rail loading arms are listed from 2" to 6" and marine arms in 6" and 8", depending on the type. The line size is chosen for the flow rate the bay needs.

items.q: What is a double bottom-loading arm?
items.a: Two arms on one column: one carries the liquid to the tanker and the other returns displaced vapour, so the tanker can be loaded with vapour recovery.

items.q: Can a loading arm be lined with PTFE?
items.a: Yes. PTFE-lined arms and swivel joints are used for corrosive chemicals and for food and pharmaceutical products where the wetted surface must be inert.

items.q: Are loading arms built to order?
items.a: Yes. Each arm is configured for the product, line size, reach, connection height and end fitting of the bay, so send those details with your enquiry.

hero.intro: Fixed loading platforms with folding stairs give operators safe access to the top of road tankers, rail cars and containers for top loading, sampling and inspection. A safety cage or basket lowers around the hatch area to guard against a fall from height. Stairs, cages and platforms are built to the bay's height, tanker range and layout.

guidance.heading: Stairs, cage or full-length basket?
guidance.body: Folding stairs (three, four or five rungs) bridge the gap between the platform and the tanker walkway. A safety cage guards a single hatch; a long-distance or full-length safety basket covers several hatches along the tanker with railings and floor trapdoors. A platform with canopy adds a sheltered working area at the bay.

items.q: How is the number of stair rungs chosen?
items.a: By the height difference between the platform and the tanker tops the bay serves. Fewer rungs suit a narrow range of tanker heights; more rungs cover a wider range.

items.q: Can access stairs and cages be combined with a loading arm?
items.a: Yes. Platforms are often built with the loading arm, stairs and safety cage as one bay layout so the operator reaches the hatch and the arm from the same position.

items.q: What information is needed to quote a loading platform?
items.a: The bay length, the range of tanker heights and hatch positions, how many hatches must be reached, whether a canopy is needed, and any site standard for handrails and finish.

hero.intro: Systems that measure, protect and clean a loading operation: skid-mounted metering systems that measure product delivered to tankers and rail cars, grounding and overfill monitors that stop bottom loading if a tanker is not earthed or a compartment is full, and pigging systems that clear product from transfer lines between batches.

items.q: What does a pigging system do in a loading terminal?
items.a: It pushes a pig through the transfer line to recover product and clean the line between batches, reducing product loss and cross-contamination when one line serves several products.

items.q: Why is a grounding and overfill monitor used for bottom loading?
items.a: It proves the tanker is earthed before loading starts and stops the flow if an overfill sensor trips, protecting against static ignition and overfilling.

  • Articulated design with swivel joints to follow the movement needed at connection
  • Counterweight balancing so the operator can position the arm with little effort
  • Self-supporting construction, sized to the project loads

  • Barge and river-vessel transfer
  • Marine terminals handling hydrocarbons and chemicals

faqs.answer: A marine loading arm is an articulated pipe assembly that links shore piping to a ship, barge or river-vessel manifold. This version is balanced by a counterweight, so the operator can move it into position with little effort. It is used at ports, jetties and river terminals for loading and unloading.

faqs.question: What materials is a marine loading arm built from?

faqs.question: How does counterweight balancing work on a marine loading arm?
faqs.answer: A counterweight offsets the weight of the arm so that it stays where it is placed and can be moved with little effort. The manufacturer data lists counterweight balancing for this arm, while the web page also mentions other balance types. Confirm the balance system you need at enquiry.

faqs.question: Which connections can a marine loading arm have at the vessel end?

faqs.question: Which options can be added to a marine loading arm?
faqs.answer: Options on request are a shut-off valve, purge and drain system, insulating flange, vapour return line, breakaway coupling or emergency release system, instrumentation and parking locks. Which ones are needed depends on the product and the terminal safety philosophy. List them in the enquiry.

faqs.question: What affects the reach and envelope of a marine loading arm?
faqs.answer: Reach, connection height, orientation and operating envelope are configured for each project from the manifold position and the vessel movement. River or tide level range matters because the arm must follow the manifold up and down. Send a layout drawing with the level range.

faqs.question: How does a marine loading arm differ from a hose reel for marine transfer?
faqs.answer: A loading arm is a rigid articulated pipe on swivel joints, while a hose reel stores and pays out a flexible hose. The arm gives a fixed envelope and is balanced to hold position, whereas a [hose reel](/c/lay-flat-hose-reels-winders) suits shorter, lighter hose connections. The choice depends on size and movement.

faqs.question: How should a marine loading arm be inspected and handled?
faqs.answer: Check the swivel joints, seals and balancing for free movement and leakage regularly, and park the arm when it is not connected. Inspection intervals and seal replacement follow the project engineering data. Ask at quotation for the maintenance information that goes with the arm.

faqs.question: What is a metal expansion joint and what does it do in piping?
faqs.answer: A metal expansion joint is a flexible bellows section that absorbs thermal growth, vibration and misalignment in a pipe run. It reduces the stress on pipes and on connected equipment such as pumps. It is used in power, refinery and process plants.

faqs.question: What sizes do metal expansion joints with stainless bellows come in?
faqs.answer: The range runs from DN 50 to DN 3000. Pick the nominal diameter to match the pipe, then size the bellows for the movement and the pressure. The catalogue gives no size table, so every joint is made to order from your data.

faqs.question: What types of metal expansion joint are available?
faqs.answer: The types are axial, angular, lateral and universal, in single or multi-ply bellows. Axial joints take movement along the pipe, angular joints take rotation and lateral joints take sideways offset. Universal joints combine movements. The choice follows the pipe layout and anchoring.

faqs.question: What bellows materials are used in metal expansion joints?
faqs.answer: Bellows are made in stainless steel 304, 304L, 316, 316L or 321, or in Inconel. End fittings are carbon steel, stainless steel, cast or forged. Choose the grade from the medium, temperature and corrosion risk, and state them at enquiry.

faqs.question: What pressure rating does a metal expansion joint have?
faqs.answer: The catalogue does not give a fixed rating: nominal pressure is set per request, together with the movement and temperature. A multi-ply bellows or pressure-balanced design is used where the pressure thrust requires it. State your design pressure and test pressure when enquiring.

faqs.question: When are tie rods, hinges or gimbals fitted to an expansion joint?
faqs.answer: Tie rods, hinges, gimbals or pressure balancing are added where the movement and pressure thrust require them. They restrain the joint so the bellows only moves in the intended direction. Say whether the line is anchored so the correct restraint can be specified.

faqs.question: What end connections can a metal expansion joint have?
faqs.answer: End connections are weld ends to ISO or flanges to DIN EN 1092-1, or as specified. Match them to the mating pipe or flange, and give the flange pressure class for a flanged joint. Matching [industrial flanges](/c/industrial-flanges) can be quoted with the joint.

faqs.question: What tests are listed for metal expansion joints?
faqs.answer: The catalogue lists in-house hydrostatic, dye penetrant, fatigue and helium leak testing. Which tests apply to a given order, and what documents are issued, is confirmed at quotation. State the test and documentation you need in the enquiry.

faqs.question: How does a lateral expansion joint differ from an axial one?
faqs.answer: An axial joint absorbs movement along the pipe axis, while a lateral joint absorbs sideways offset between two pipe ends. Give the direction and size of movement for each. If your project differs from the listed data, tell us and we will confirm what can be supplied.
